claims.statement: Denton scheduled two public hearings on a proposed data-center moratorium for September 22 and October 27, 2026.
claims.text: Denton scheduled two public hearings on a proposed data-center moratorium for September 22 and October 27, 2026.
claims.quote: The City will hold two public hearings on September 22, 2026, and October 27, 2026
claims.value_text: Denton scheduled two public hearings on a proposed data-center moratorium for September 22 and October 27, 2026.
claims.scope_note: The notice schedules hearings; it does not show a moratorium in force.

claims.statement: Denton held the first hearing on September 22, and the council took no vote that night.
claims.text: Denton held the first hearing on September 22, and the council took no vote that night.
claims.quote: The Denton City Council held the first of two required public hearings on the proposed moratorium. No vote was taken on Tuesday.
claims.value_text: Denton held the first hearing on September 22, and the council took no vote that night.
claims.scope_note: The source reports the meeting result; Legistar has no final-action entry.

claims.statement: All 20 people who spoke at the September 22 hearing supported the proposed pause.
claims.text: All 20 people who spoke at the September 22 hearing supported the proposed pause.
claims.quote: All 20 people who spoke during the hearing supported the moratorium
claims.value_text: All 20 people who spoke at the September 22 hearing supported the proposed pause.
claims.scope_note: This counts meeting speakers, not all Denton residents.

claims.statement: If approved, the moratorium would temporarily halt Denton acceptance, processing and approval of new data-center applications, without affecting already approved projects.
claims.text: If approved, the moratorium would temporarily halt Denton acceptance, processing and approval of new data-center applications, without affecting already approved projects.
claims.quote: If approved, the moratorium would temporarily halt the city’s acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for new data center developments. It would not affect projects that have already been approved.
claims.value_text: If approved, the moratorium would temporarily halt Denton acceptance, processing and approval of new data-center applications, without affecting already approved projects.
claims.scope_note: Conditional proposal, not a rule currently in effect.

claims.statement: City staff warned that Denton electric transmission is near capacity and proposed roughly $300 million in transmission projects while awaiting ERCOT response.
claims.text: City staff warned that Denton electric transmission is near capacity and proposed roughly $300 million in transmission projects while awaiting ERCOT response.
claims.quote: City staff have warned that the system is already operating near capacity. Denton Municipal Electric has proposed roughly $300 million in transmission projects to address the issue and is awaiting a response
claims.value_text: City staff warned that Denton electric transmission is near capacity and proposed roughly $300 million in transmission projects while awaiting ERCOT response.
claims.scope_note: A proposal and staff warning, not a measured household bill impact or completed project.

claims.statement: Denton Mayor Chris Watts said people could still seek to place another data center until a moratorium is in place.
claims.text: Denton Mayor Chris Watts said people could still seek to place another data center until a moratorium is in place.
claims.quote: until it’s in place, people can still contact people, people can still try to find a way to place another data center here
claims.value_text: Denton Mayor Chris Watts said people could still seek to place another data center until a moratorium is in place.
claims.scope_note: His quote describes opportunity to seek a site, not evidence of a specific application after the hearing.

claims.statement: On September 21, the governor directed TCEQ to halt permits sought by data centers until ERCOT completes its audit, and said state agencies should not advance related approvals until required information is acquired.
claims.text: On September 21, the governor directed TCEQ to halt permits sought by data centers until ERCOT completes its audit, and said state agencies should not advance related approvals until required information is acquired.
claims.quote: directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to halt all permits sought by data centers until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes its audit. Because the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT), ERCOT, and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) require that information to make informed decisions, no state agency shall move forward with regulatory approvals related to data center development until it is acquired.
claims.value_text: state TCEQ permits halted pending ERCOT audit
claims.scope_note: This state directive is separate from the unadopted Denton local moratorium; it does not show that all construction stopped.

claims.text: The city hearing transcript records blue cards from people wishing to speak during the September 22 data-center hearing.

rejected: No Denton moratorium was enacted at the first hearing.
Twenty speakers are meeting participants, not a citywide survey.
No specific post-hearing application, permit approval, blackout, or household bill change is documented.
Do not imply Denton local applications or all construction can proceed unrestricted while the separate state permit halt applies.
